headline: Committee discussed bridge repairs, scheduled a gatehouse inspection, and reviewed plans for a proposed 2030 pedestrian bridge at the Tannery site.
summary: The committee reviewed updates on committee membership and bridge repairs at Mill Pond and North 7th Street. A structural engineer site walk for the Gatehouse was scheduled for September 11, 2026. The committee also discussed access routes, design, and maintenance plans for a proposed 2030 pedestrian bridge connecting to the old Tannery site.

plain_text:
Mine Falls Park Trail Committee - September 8, 2026 
Mine Falls Park Trail Committee — Meeting Minutes from Sept 8th-2026. 
Attendees: Kamal Masand, Lon Humberger, Ben Davis, Andrew Lucci, Justin Hoprich, Steven Kenney, Natalie 
Lucci, Paula Lochhead, Bryan Conant. 
1. Call to Order & Approval of Minutes=7:00 PM. 
• Motion made and seconded to approve the previous meeting's minutes. The motion passed. 
 
2. Committee Updates & Personnel Changes 
• Flora is returning and will resume attending meetings. 
• Matt Roscoe is leaving the committee due to time conflicts. The chair thanked him for his service. 
• The committee will follow up with the city (Greg) to update the member list on the city website. 
 
3. Bridge Repairs & Inspections 
• Mill Pond Bridges: Minor safety repairs have been completed. A structural engineer may be needed to 
inspect the wooden structures and stone abutments due to their age and remaining service life. 
• North 7th Street Bridge: Recommendations are pending from Hoyle Tanner regarding the bridge 
flooring/surface. Discussion included the potential use of expanded metal or sub-surface metal beneath the 
wooden boards. 
• Gatehouse Inspection: A site walk with structural engineer Jason Gallant (Wright-Pierce) is scheduled for 
Friday, September 11, 2026, at 11:00 AM to assess the entire building (roof, soffits, moisture issues). A 
summary report will be requested before the next BPW meeting on September 24th. 
 
4. Proposed 2030 Pedestrian Bridge (Tannery Site Connection) 
• Access & Route: Representatives from Community Development explored access options. The proposed 
route enters via the access road near the cell towers, runs along the back of Soccer Field 4, and crosses over 
to the old Tannery site. 
• Design & Specs: Due to elevation differences, the bridge landing will likely feature an elevated 
boardwalk/ramp. Construction must be ADA-compliant. 
• Trail Impact & Maintenance: The committee discussed potential traffic increases, trail widening (crushed 
gravel vs. asphalt), clearing brush for visibility and safety, and clarifying maintenance responsibilities (snow 
removal, trail upkeep) between the city and housing/property management. 
• Adjournment : 801 pm
